items.title: Kenny Davern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: An example of how that could get screwed up was Henry “Red” Allen... he yells, “George Washington.”... He says, “The bridge, the bridge.”

ctx.x: Right. Or it could mean, in some instances, theme song. The T. But in a jazz band, that would mean bridge in some circles. An example of how that could get screwed up was Henry “Red” Allen, who loved to work in a quartet format, went out to Detroit to play a club, no it was Cleveland. Went to Cleveland to play the Theatrical Lounge. And he had locals. And he was playing a tune, “Rosetta” or whatever it was, and he wanted to take it out. So he yells, “George Washington.” And you know the band comes back and…
Washington bridge in Cleveland. So there, Monk, is an example of how that completely turned around.
